I am a 60-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with primary schooling. I have farmed these lands for over 40 years, and I know what works here on the North China Plain. I hold about 10 mu of land, and I will plant my main 8-mu plot with the double-cropping system we have always relied on: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I am not growing cotton this year — at my age, the 16-plus spray rounds and hand pruning that cotton demands are too much for my back. Wheat and maize can be handled with machines, and the inputs are predictable.

For wheat, I will rotary-till the soil in early October and sow improved seeds — Luyuan502 has done well for me in recent years. I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a basal dose, then topdress with urea at green-up in spring. Water is precious, so I irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, and twice in spring at jointing and grain-filling. I spray four times total — insecticide twice, herbicide once, and fungicide once — because aphids and powdery mildew come every year. I expect around 1,000 jin per mu, which is 500 kg.

For maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seeds right after the wheat harvest in June. I do not till for maize — no-tillage planting into the wheat stubble saves diesel and time when the heat is worst. I put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. Two irrigations are enough: one when the plants are knee-high, and one at filling. Four pesticide applications keep the borers and weeds under control. I expect about 1,200 jin per mu, which is 600 kg.

This is the system I trust. It feeds my household, the inputs are available at the village supply store, and I can manage the labor myself.
